t:
(a) In General.—The Secretary of Defense shall inform members of the Armed Forces, using mechanisms available to the Secretary, of the eligibility of such members for services of the Department of Veterans Affairs relating to sexual trauma. 
    (b) Information From Sexual Assault Response Coordinators.—The Secretary of Defense shall ensure—
        (1) that Sexual Assault Response Coordinators and uniformed victims advocates of the Department of Defense advise members of the Armed Forces who report instances of sexual trauma regarding the eligibility of such members for services at the Department of Veterans Affairs; and 
        (2) that such information is included in mandatory training materials.  
    (c) Sexual Trauma Defined.—In this section, the term “sexual trauma” means psychological trauma described in section 1720D(a)(1) of title 38, United States Code.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that advising and informing service members is a form of outreach or consultation. It fails because the section only pushes information one way, from the Department of Defense to members of the Armed Forces, about their eligibility for VA services. No party outside the federal government is consulted or given a role in any federal decision, and there is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue.
fable.s: The Secretary of Defense shall inform members of the Armed Forces, using mechanisms available to the Secretary, of the eligibility of such members for services of the Department of Veterans Affairs relating to sexual trauma.

opus.w: This section only requires the Department of Defense to tell service members which Veterans Affairs sexual-trauma services they qualify for, and to put that information in training materials. Nobody is asked for input, so no consultation, comment period, hearing or advisory body feeds into a federal decision. The word "advise" here means DoD staff passing information to service members, all of whom are inside the federal government. It is not outside parties advising the government.
opus.s: The Secretary of Defense shall inform members of the Armed Forces, using mechanisms available to the Secretary, of the eligibility of such members for services of the Department of Veterans Affairs relating to sexual trauma.
opus.b: The tempting reading is that this is participation because Sexual Assault Response Coordinators and victims advocates "advise members of the Armed Forces." That reading fails on two counts. First, the information only flows one way: the Department of Defense tells service members which services they qualify for, and no federal decision depends on their input. Second, everyone involved (the Secretary, the coordinators, uniformed advocates and service members) is inside the federal government.

qwen_chat.w: This section requires the Secretary of Defense to inform members of the Armed Forces about their eligibility for VA services. Members of the Armed Forces are federal employees/officials, which places them inside the federal government boundary. Furthermore, this is a one-way notification regarding benefit eligibility, not a consultation, coordination, or advisory process involving outside parties in a federal decision-making process.
qwen_chat.s: The Secretary of Defense shall inform members of the Armed Forces, using mechanisms available to the Secretary, of the eligibility of such members for services of the Department of Veterans Affairs relating to sexual trauma.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that informing members of the Armed Forces constitutes "participation" because it involves communication with people outside the immediate decision-making body of the Secretary. However, members of the Armed Forces are federal employees/officials (inside the government), and merely informing them of eligibility for benefits is not "consultation" or "coordination" before a decision, nor is it an advisory role. It is an administrative notification.
